newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude markets firm in brisk January trad.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude markets firm in brisk January trad.

text.p: North Sea physical crude differentials firmed on Wednesday, but while Brent intermonth spreads held earlier gains, outright prices eased lower.
Several North Sea grades traded at steady to firmer numbers with two Forties cargoes, loading Jan 4-6 and Jan 6-8, fetching Dated Brent +28 cents.

After four cargoes were sold on Tuesday, traders said that the first decade Forties programme was virtually sold out and some expected differentials for second decade cargoes to command a premium of more than 30 cents to Dated Brent.
A Statfjord cargo loading Jan 8-10 traded at Dated Brent +28 cents, 10 cents above the price of a December-loading cargo traded late last week.
Other Norwegian grades also fetched stronger numbers, with a Dec 7-9 Troll sold at Dated Brent +40 cents and a Dec 7-9 Gullfaks C traded at Dated +37.5 cents.

A Dec 27-29 Brent was sold earlier to a Wall Street trader for Jan Brent -18.5 cents, but late Dec and early Jan barrels were assessed at or above Jan -12/13 cents later in line with next week's cfds which made further gains to talk around Feb Brent +40 cents.
Feb Brent paper fell back sharply after trading early at $23.73 a barrel to talk some 35-40 cents down at $23.30/$23.35 in line with IPE screen levels at 1645 GMT.
But intermonth spreads held earlier gains with Jan/Feb talked either side of +55 cents and Feb/March at +63/64.
